title: Recipe Matching from a Contiguous Ingredient Run
description_html:
You are given an ordered list of ingredients and several recipes, where each recipe is a sequence of ingredients. For each recipe, determine whether it can be formed by a contiguous run of the ingredient list — i.e. whether the recipe appears as a contiguous substring of the ingredient sequence.

Output

For each recipe, output whether it is a contiguous subsequence of the ingredient list (true/false).

Approaches

  • Prefix / rolling hash — fingerprint the ingredient list so any window compares in O(1); match each recipe by hash (verify on hit).
  • Follow-up 1 (O(1) extra space) — two-pointer / sliding-window scan comparing element by element.
  • Follow-up 2 (streaming, large volume) — feed ingredients through a state machine (KMP per recipe, or Aho-Corasick for all recipes at once) and match on the fly.

Example

ingredients = [A, B, C, D, E]
recipes:
  [B, C, D]  -> true   (contiguous run)
  [A, C]     -> false  (A,C not contiguous)
  [D, E]     -> true

This is multi-pattern substring matching (equivalent to LC 1408 / 28). See Notes for all three approaches, the trio, and references.
